strategy.summary: Buy stock index futures around the turn of the month, day session only. McConnell & Xu (2008) find that the last trading day of a month and the first three of the next carried essentially all of the US equity premium from 1926 to 2005, which they and later work (Etula et al. 2020) tie to month-end pension, payroll and fund flows. Evidence for S&P futures in recent decades is mixed, and most published numbers are close-to-close, overnight included; this run keeps only the day session, because nothing is held overnight.
strategy.formula: Long on the month's last N and the next month's first M trading days, entry time to exit time

rules.label: Days
rules.text: The last 1, 2, 3 or 4 NYSE trading days of the month and/or the first 1, 2 or 3 of the next (either side may be none, not both), each day its own trade. Optional filter: skip scheduled FOMC statement days.

rules.label: Enter
rules.text: Buy at 09:30, 10:00, 10:30, 11:00, 12:00, 13:00, 14:00 or 15:00 ET, at that minute's open. The day is skipped if the bars have a gap of more than 5 minutes there.

rules.label: Exit
rules.text: Sell at 12:00, 13:00, 15:00, 15:30 or 16:00 ET (only exits after the entry are tested), at the close of the minute before. On early-close days the trade closes at the last bar. Optional stop 0.25%, 0.5% or 1% below the entry price, live during the trade.

rules.label: Size
rules.text: One position at a time, never held overnight. As many whole ES contracts as the account covers at full contract value (no leverage), starting from $1,000,000.

axes.label: First N days of next month

strategy.length_note: Times are New York clock times on 1-minute bars from 08:00 to 17:00 ET.

funnel.name: Start
funnel.why: All 4,864 versions backtested once on 2018–2022 data.

funnel.name: 1 · Integrity
funnel.why: Per-trade checks on every version: the month-end day count, the FOMC and auction days and the entry and exit bars were recomputed independently; each trade was long, on one of the month's last trading days with the filter met, entered and exited at the set times; no eligible day was skipped; fills were never better than the market; nothing was held overnight. Plus 40 random versions re-run on cut-off data. 0 failed.

funnel.name: 2 · Enough trades
funnel.why: Needs ≥100 completed trades and ≥10 a year in ≥4 of the 5 years. Removed 512 (512 on 1min).

funnel.name: 3 · Profit
funnel.why: Needs a net profit, Sharpe ≥ 0.75 and drawdown no worse than 30%. Removed 4,282 (4,282 on 1min); 2,231 of them lost money.

funnel.name: 4 · Stable settings
funnel.why: Each setting is nudged one at a time, down and up: the entry time by ±30 minutes, the exit time by ±15 minutes and the number of month-end days by ±1, the number of next-month days by ±1 and a stop by ±0.1% ("no stop" has nothing to nudge). At least 70% of the nudged versions must be profitable, with median Sharpe ≥ 0.5. Removed 5.

funnel.name: 6 · Remove duplicates
funnel.why: Versions whose monthly returns correlate ≥ 0.8 form a group; the best 2 of each go on (a group of one keeps its one). 65 versions formed 22 groups; 38 of the 38 picks are distinct backtests.

funnel.name: 8 · Validation
funnel.why: Frozen finalists run once on unseen data: needs net > 0, Sharpe ≥ 0.3, drawdown no worse than 30% and ≥40 trades.

luck.method: Per clock and stop (entry time x exit rule x stop): the same long trade at the same clock, but on random validation-window NYSE trading days that are not among the month's last 5 or first 4 trading days. The number of days is scaled so the time in market matches each level. Same fills, slippage, commission and whole-contract sizing as the strategy; scored with the same daily-Sharpe and time-in-market code.
luck.text: For every whole-percent time in market in each group's 2023–2024 range, 100 placebo runs buy ES at the same clock (same entry and exit times) but on random ordinary days: never among the month's last 5 or first 4 trading days. So they test whether the month-end calendar matters, or whether the same hours on any day would have done as well. Each group is one entry-and-exit clock and stop setting. They pay the same costs and use the same sizing and Sharpe math as the strategy.

assumptions: Data: Databento CME continuous front month (ES.v.0), 1-minute bars from 08:00 to 17:00 ET only. Rolls are back-adjusted; positions never cross a session.
Costs: 1 tick slippage per side and $2.50 commission per contract per side.

Every published month-end figure is close-to-close and includes the overnight session. This run measures only the day-session part; failing here means that part is too small, not that the month-end effect is gone.

Month-turn days come from the NYSE calendar. This ES grid was specified after the ZN month-end run (me_zn_v1) failed validation; its day-session results (morning entries best, afternoons worst) were seen before this grid was set.
Long only on a calendar: part of every version's profit is the market's own upward drift. The placebo test (same clock on ordinary days) separates the calendar from that drift.
Each trade uses the whole account in whole contracts with no leverage, the same as the other families.
Sharpe uses daily mark-to-market returns (√252), with idle cash earning 0%. Time in market is the share of 1-minute bars with an open position.
Other strategy families were already selected on this market's 2023–2024 data, so 2023–2024 is not untouched; only the 2025+ holdout is.
Holdout (2025 onward) was run once for #1, #7, #17; the results are on this market's separate holdout tab.
